title: Self-Ext to dual self-Tor cap comparison on regular affine charts
statement: For any closed immersion i:Z -> Y [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme], natural number n and derived category of module sheaves on Y [def-pc-derived-category], let B=i_*O_Z, G=H^n(RHom_Y(B[0],B[0])) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and Q=i*H^{-n}(B[0] tensor^L B[0]), using the fixed derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure, def-pc-module-pullback]. There exists a global morphism kappa: i*G -> dual(Q) [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For every open V of Z and affine U of Y whose immersion ideal is spanned by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], its restriction to V and then to the over site of V intersect i^{-1}(U) is an isomorphism [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No conormal comparison or overlap compatibility is asserted.

source.place: duality.tex, lemma-regular-ideal-ext: Hom of the Koszul resolution into the quotient and zero differential. Tag 08DH, cohomology.tex, derived internal Hom/evaluation; Tag 068G, more-algebra.tex, equation-simple-tor-product, tensor of resolutions for Tor.

proof.text: Apply exists_selfExt_tor_resolution_model to obtain common complexes T and J, the pure degree-zero cohomology of J, the structure-sheaf identification e0, the Ext and Tor identifications eG and eQ, and all regular-chart zero-differential models.

Use the uniquely cycle-characterized homologyEvaluation of T against J. Apply the internal Hom bifunctor to the Tor isomorphism contravariantly and the degree-zero isomorphism covariantly, obtaining an isomorphism eD into dual Q. Define the existential witness by the composite eG.hom followed by evaluation followed by eD.hom.

For a chosen V and regular affine U, use the model theorem to get K-injectivity of the restricted J and a finite free zero model of the restricted T. homologyEvaluation_isIso gives invertibility of restricted evaluation. Restriction and over-site functors preserve the two comparison isomorphisms. Expand their functor images using map_comp and compose the three isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem selfExt_tor_dual_chart
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (n : ℕ) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let G := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (n : ℤ)).obj
        (H.obj (op (S.obj B), S.obj B))
    let Q := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (-(n : ℤ))).obj
          (S.obj B ⊗ S.obj B))
    ∃ κ : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj G ⟶ Scheme.Modules.dual Q,
      ∀ (V : Z.Opens) (U : Y.affineOpens)
        (_hU : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1)),
          Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U ∧
            RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f),
        IsIso (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).map κ).over
          (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)))
